Thought: To determine which of these compounds is the least acidic, we need to consider the effect of the substituents (Br, Cl, F, I) on the acidity of the carboxylic acids. The acidity of a compound is influenced by the electron-withdrawing ability of the substituent. More electronegative substituents increase acidity by stabilizing the negative charge on the carboxylate ion. The order of electronegativity for the halogens is F > Cl > Br > I. Therefore, the compound with the least electronegative substituent will be the least acidic. Among the given options, iodine (I) is the least electronegative, so ICH2CO2H should be the least acidic compound.
